questions.q: Why can't the Master (rank 0) pod safely run on a spot instance without extra handling, while a Worker pod can?
options: Master pods require more GPU memory than spot instances provide
The Master anchors the rendezvous address and drives checkpoint writes, so losing its node loses the entire job's coordination point, not just one worker's GPUs
Spot instances cannot run containers at all
AWS does not allow rank-0 processes on spot instances by policy
questions.explain: The Master plays a distinguished coordination role. If its node is reclaimed, the whole job loses the point everything else was rendezvousing through — a much larger blast radius than losing an individual Worker.

questions.q: Roughly how much advance warning does AWS give before actually terminating a spot instance, and what is the practical implication?
options: About 2 minutes — short enough that only an automated response can react in time
About 24 hours — long enough for a human to manually intervene
No warning at all is ever given
Exactly 500 training steps worth of time
questions.explain: AWS's spot interruption notice gives roughly 2 minutes before termination. That window is far too short for human reaction time, so any handling of it has to be fully automated.

questions.q: Why does Solara AI's interruption-handling code trigger an emergency checkpoint save immediately upon seeing the interruption notice, rather than waiting for the next scheduled checkpoint?
options: Because scheduled checkpoints are disabled when running on spot instances
Because the instance may be terminated before the next ~500-step/~30-minute scheduled checkpoint would occur, so an out-of-cycle save is the only way to capture progress before losing the node
Because emergency checkpoints are smaller and faster than scheduled ones
Because AWS requires an emergency checkpoint before allowing any spot termination
questions.explain: The ~2-minute interruption window could occur at any point between scheduled checkpoints, potentially discarding up to ~30 minutes of progress if nothing is done — triggering an immediate save minimizes that loss.

questions.q: Why is a roughly 60-90% cost discount typically available for spot/preemptible instances in the first place?
options: Cloud providers lose money on spot instances deliberately as a promotional strategy
The provider is selling capacity that would otherwise sit idle, on the condition it can reclaim it on short notice if a higher-paying customer needs it
Spot instances use older, slower hardware than on-demand instances
The discount only applies to instances with no GPU attached
questions.explain: Spot/preemptible pricing monetizes otherwise-idle capacity. The discount exists specifically because the customer accepts the risk of losing that capacity with little warning.

questions.q: Why is the GCP preemption notice (around 30 seconds) more operationally demanding to handle than AWS's spot interruption notice (around 2 minutes)?
options: It isn't more demanding — the two are functionally identical in every respect
The much shorter window leaves less time for an emergency checkpoint's parallel, sharded write to complete before the instance is actually reclaimed
GCP preemptible VMs cannot run GPU workloads at all
GCP requires manual approval before any checkpoint can be saved
questions.explain: A shorter advance-warning window means the emergency checkpoint save has less time to complete before the node disappears, making the margin for error tighter on GCP than on AWS.
